title: Multiple Variable Declarations and Assignments
learningObjectives: Declare multiple variables of the same type in one declaration.
Declare variables of different types using separate declarations.
Use assignment chaining with compatible types.
Use tuple deconstruction to assign multiple values in one statement.
Swap two variables using tuple assignment and explain evaluation order.

understand.concept: C# allows multiple declarators of the same type in one local declaration. Variables of different types normally use separate declarations. Assignment expressions can be chained, and tuple deconstruction can assign several variables from a tuple in one statement.
understand.whyItMatters: Working with related values is common in calculations, records and algorithms. Knowing the available syntax helps keep declarations concise without hiding types or evaluation order.
understand.analogy: Multiple declarations are like writing several labelled entries on one form. Tuple deconstruction is like unpacking a small bundle into separate variables.
understand.analogyLimit: The syntax does not make the variables a collection. Each declared variable remains independent and has its own type and scope.

explain.narrative:
## Multiple declarators

A declaration can contain more than one variable of the same explicit type, separated by commas. Each variable is distinct and can have its own initializer.

## Different types

Use separate declarations for unrelated types so each type is clear. The var keyword also has restrictions: an implicitly typed local declaration cannot declare multiple variables in one declaration.

## Chained assignment

Assignment expressions associate from right to left. In a chained assignment, the rightmost assignment is evaluated first and its resulting value is assigned to the variable on the left. Use this only when the shared value and types make the intent obvious.

## Tuple deconstruction

A tuple can provide multiple values for deconstruction. Existing variables can also receive a tuple assignment. This is useful for swapping values without a temporary variable.

## Version baseline

Tuple deconstruction is supported from C# 7 onward. All examples use C# 14 and .NET 10.
